title.narrative: Deregulation to foster private sector development in Ukraine

description.narrative: The project supports Ukraine in using a window of opportunity to revise its existing business regulations for the dynamization of the private sector development and local entrepreneurship in the current war situation. In doing so, the project facilitates the adoption and full and timely implementation of deregulatory changes of existing legislation by: i) enabling the dialogue and cooperation between public and private stakeholders in the country; ii) providing strategic advice on communication and policy advocacy to local private sector organizations; iii) supporting the advocacy by the regulatory policy analysis and impact assessment. The project has a positive impact on:SDG 8: inclusive and sustainable economic growth: support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation.

comment.narrative:
Public sector: The project supported 14 ministries and 7 central executive bodies. Private sector : Regulations that are to be changed or abolished potentially reach 197 thousand legal entities and 735 private entrepreneurs that belong to about 300 economic activities / markets (counted as NACE codes). Regulation compliance costs for businesses are about 4%. Updated and more simplified and efficient regulations in the economic sphere reduce the costs of the entrepreneurs and of the state in business development; and reduces the possibility of corruption.
The project has provided technical support to the Ukrainian public and private organizatrions with the following activities: • CES processed more than 1000 regulations, shortlisted by the Ministry in cooperation with two other think tanks (BRDO and CER( that work with the ministry on deregulation. • Setting up and facilitating deregulation seventeen (17) working groups focusing on: i) regulations of Ministry of Finance; and one with the regulations related to compulsory insurance, with the National Bank and 14 ministries of Ukraine. . • Participation in 10 expert group sessions (where preliminary discissions took place, before working group sessions). PO-CES has provided advice of what to do with regulations, checked them for EU compatibility, calculated possible impact, participated in discussions with issuers of regulations (who often tried to keep their regulations intact). • Continuous communications with both public and private stakeholders during the technical assistance phase. • Organization of a public event where the results of the project were presented. In this event, the Ministry of Economy also presented the results of the first phase of the deregulation campaign (2023) and declared the transition to second one, that would be permanent, more focused on regulations that affect businesses the most, and with more inclusive down to up approach. title.narrative: Description of changes achieved in laws, regulations, policy plans, outcomes of social dialogue or development strategies enacted or adopted by local government or social dialogue partners, yielding tangible benefits to the business climate

comment.narrative:
Ukraine started full-scale deregulation campaigns eight years ago. During 2016-2019, more than 3,000 regulations were analyzed, of then 850 abolished and even more changed. The need for deregulation is primarily driven by the complexity of the regulatory environment for local economic development in the context of the ongoing war; and also by the ambition of the country to become a member state of the European Union. There are about 85,000 regulatory acts in Ukraine and which 40,000 regulations are related to business activities.
The results of this project contributed with identification and analysis of regulations shortlisted by the Ministry of Economy of Ukraine. • As a result, 235 regulations were cancelled, 537 were amended, 238 were retained; and 54 policy instruments have been cancelled. According to CES’s calculations, regulations that are to be abolished or changed affect about 300 markets (counted as NACE codes). • In economic terms, as of the beginning of 2023, there were 197 thousand legal entities and 735 thousand private entrepreneurs, in total having almost 5 million of people involved. According to the forecast of the Ministry of Economic Development and Trade (which CES also participated), the savings for businesses as a result of deregulation in five sectors alone (agriculture, construction, energy, IT/Telecoms, and Minecon regulation spheres) would be about UAH 10.5 billion (approx.. 274 Million Euro). The project also contributed with concrete short term recommendations to the government; i) focus on regulations that have larger impact (or at least reach, if the impact cannot be calculated) ii) favor bottom to up approach, iii) make decisions favoring businesses. In the long run (i.e. after the end of the martial law) CES recommended to calculate all the costs of regulations and to state explicit cost reduction goals.
